$description: LAYER 1 — Dark semantic colors. Keep primary aligned with light. Add aliases needed by Layer 2 dark component tokens.

white.$description: On the dark page "white" is the surface color: every MFE surface written as white or bg-white (headers, cards, form sections, Studio outline) follows the dark surface. Text or borders that must stay white use #FFFFFF (scripts/sync-dark-tokens.js does that for the dark twins) → --pgn-color-white

500.$description: Dark twin of the light token (scripts/sync-dark-tokens.js). Paragon default → --pgn-color-primary-500

700.$description: Dark twin of the light token (scripts/sync-dark-tokens.js). Paragon default → --pgn-color-primary-700

base.$description: LAYER 1 color 1 — Primary on dark surfaces.

light.$description: Primary-tinted surface for row/trigger hover on dark: primary mixed 88% into the page color, so it follows the primary and page colors → --pgn-color-primary-light

hover.$description: Marketing primary hover on dark surfaces → --pgn-color-primary-hover (best-effort — no dark Lovable reference)

soft.$description: Marketing primary tint surface on dark → --pgn-color-primary-soft (best-effort — no dark Lovable reference)

base.$description: LAYER 1 color 2 — Secondary on dark surfaces.

light.$description: Secondary-tinted surface on dark: secondary mixed 88% into the page color → --pgn-color-secondary-light

base.$description: Brand follows Layer 1 Primary on dark.

light.$description: Secondary text on dark (catalog meta, course card details) → --pgn-color-text-light

primary.$description: Secondary text on dark (authn tabs fallback) → --pgn-color-text-primary

inverse.$description: Text, border or icon on a colored or dark backdrop; the one place white is written in the dark theme (color.white is the surface color) → --pgn-color-text-inverse

black.$description: On the dark page "black" is the page text color: the MFEs write strong text (Studio page titles, section headers, help sidebar titles) as black. Text that must stay dark on a light or colored surface uses {color.bg.base} → --pgn-color-black
